Usage: rer VERB [FLAGS]

  rer dev <repo> [--dir DIR]      Clone, install, set up a local owner and start the app.
  rer setup <repo> [--dir DIR]    Clone, install and set up, then stop.
  rer install <repo> [--dir DIR]  Clone and install dependencies, then stop.
Repository: <owner>/<repo>, a GitHub HTTPS URL (with or without .git), or a git URL.
Clones into ./<repo-name>; --dir overrides. Reuses a clone with the same origin; refuses any other non-empty folder.


Inside a project (the nearest OPERATIONS.json at or above this folder, or --cwd DIR),
every verb runs that checkout's own pinned rer: the @runeditrun/rer version its package.json
pins (installed first for commands that run project code when node_modules holds another),
else its vendored scripts/rer.mjs.

  rer dev              Launch a first-party checkout with no setup steps: installs dependencies,
                       sets up a local owner and a free port when needed, starts the app and prints
                       RER_READY and a sign-in link. Without a terminal it returns once the app is
                       ready and leaves it running (--detach and --foreground override); allow up
                       to 10 minutes on a first launch, or rerun it to reattach. rer dev --stop stops it.
  rer run SCRIPT [ARGS]
                       Run a package.json script with the pnpm and Node the checkout pins (rer keeps
                       them off PATH): where a project's docs say pnpm run X, run rer run X.
  rer list [DIR]       The checkouts in DIR (default: here), newest first, with whether rer dev can
                       launch them, whether they are set up, and their running URL. --json for data.
  rer business ...     Set up your business once and share its name, logo and brand colour
                       with apps that support Business. Start with rer business connect.
  rer companion ...    Pair this computer with a Run Edit Run app and run its change requests here
                       with your own Codex or Claude. rer companion --help lists the commands.
  rer door ...         The opt-in front door: every checkout at http://NAME.localhost:PORT, started
                       on its first visit and stopped when idle. rer door --help for its verbs.
  rer cli status       This rer: version, contents digest, install channel, launcher and other rer
                       commands on PATH. --json for data.
  rer cli install      Install this package for the current user (~/.local/bin/rer).
  rer cli path         Optional: make rer available in future terminals; shows the shell step.
  rer cli uninstall    Remove the launcher and the install root; ~/.rer is untouched.
  rer update           Move to the latest published rer (--version X for an exact one), the way it
                       was installed: npx and install.sh installs switch atomically, npm installs run npm.
  rer --version        Print this rer's version; inside a checkout, also the version the checkout pins.
  rer queue NAME -- COMMAND [ARGS]
                       Run COMMAND once this computer's job queue admits it (heavy package scripts
                       of a checkout that pins the rer package use it).

Checkout verbs: install, setup, dev, preview, build, verify, reset, deploy, export, import, doctor, describe, check, adopt-edition, refresh-base, demo, signin, release, listing. Run rer VERB --help in a checkout for its flags.

Usage: rer deploy [FLAGS]
Flags: --help, --cwd, --non-interactive, --json, --owner-name, --environment, --dry-run, --site, --demo, --host, --env-file, --image, --bind-address, --http-port, --https-port, --remove, --yes, --set-secret, --unset-secret, --rotate-secret, --reopen-installation-key, --platform, --no-queue
Owner-account deployment and health; dry run builds and validates the local deployment plan, printing target names, bindings and migration names. No Cloudflare credentials or requests are needed and nothing changes remotely. Valid fixture senders on .test, .example, .invalid, .localhost and example.com, example.net or example.org (including subdomains) are accepted only in a dry run; real deploys refuse placeholder senders. Dry run never prompts for or requires a missing owner name, saves no name and bypasses custom deploy hooks and their owner-email preflight. Target secrets, permissions and remote readiness are checked only by a real deploy. Builds and deploy hooks run with the checkout's local settings files moved aside, and a build output holding one (.dev.vars, .env) is refused. Declared secrets come from the environment or --env-file (an owned 0600 KEY=VALUE file); a new Worker gets the local setup owner and fresh generated secrets when they are not given. rer keeps the secrets it generates in .rer/deploy/ENVIRONMENT.secrets.env (0600) and reuses them on every redeploy; it refuses to generate a replacement for one a live Worker holds, and --rotate-secret NAME[,NAME] replaces them on purpose. After a healthy deploy rer claims the setup owner on the hosted app with the saved setup owner name and the one-time setup token, then removes the token. For a real deploy, the managed adapter checks its hosted owner email before rer resolves the owner name, so its placeholder-email refusal comes first. If the installer declares an owner-name field and no name is saved, deploy asks once and saves it; --non-interactive requires --owner-name NAME before any upload. --set-secret NAME[,NAME] (each value from the environment or --env-file; repeat the flag or join names with commas) and --unset-secret NAME[,NAME] change those secrets of the deployed Worker without a build, all of them in one new Worker version or none, and record that version; a missing value refuses before any change. --reopen-installation-key KID temporarily binds a retired installation key from private custody, reseals restored dependency keys under the current key, verifies them and removes the previous binding. --remove --yes deletes what this environment's deploy record says rer created (Worker, D1, R2, KV, queues), reads back that each is gone, and touches nothing else. --site deploys the run site instead: an assets-only Worker on its custom domain with www redirected; with --dry-run it builds the site and prints the plan with no provider request. --demo deploys the hosted demo instead (deploy-demo.json): a front Worker on demo.<domain> giving each visitor their own signed-in, throwaway native Worker isolate of this seed with real public reads/checks and simulated external writes; --dry-run writes it to .rer/demo-host with no provider request; --demo --remove --yes deletes that demo (its Worker, demo.<domain> Custom Domain, each only while the record its deploy left proves it the demo's), reads back that each is gone, and is a no-op once it is.
probes.name: deploy-help
